en.greeting: Hi! Today is about choosing exactly the right word: words that mean the same but feel different, precise words instead of vague ones, and words that fit the tone of a text. Let's start with the feeling behind a word.

steps.title: Same meaning, different feeling
steps.text: At B2 you chose formal or informal words for the reader. Now the words are equally formal, but they feel different.
steps.body:
**Connotation** = the feeling a word carries beyond its dictionary meaning: **positive**, **neutral** or **negative**. You know it from Indonesian: *langsing*, *kurus* and *kurus kering* can describe the same body, but only *langsing* is a compliment. *Hemat* praises; *pelit* criticises the same habit.

The trap: a dictionary or Google Translate lists *kurus → thin, skinny, slim* with no feeling. Take the wrong one and you insult someone without knowing it.

steps.title: Praise or criticism?
steps.text: Here are those words in real sentences. Notice which ones praise and which ones criticise.
steps.body: `Our manager is stubborn, which really helps the team` sends two messages at once: **stubborn** criticises, but the rest of the sentence praises. Say **firm**. Careful: **mean** = stingy in British English, but usually *unkind* in American English.

examples.en: My sister is slim and very fit.
examples.id: Kakak perempuanku langsing dan sangat bugar.

examples.en: After his illness, he looked very thin.
examples.id: Setelah sakit, dia terlihat sangat kurus.

examples.en: Pak Hasan is firm with deadlines, so the team always delivers on time.
examples.id: Pak Hasan tegas soal tenggat, jadi timnya selalu menyelesaikan tepat waktu.

examples.en: He's so stubborn that he never accepts anyone else's ideas.
examples.id: Dia keras kepala sekali sampai tidak pernah menerima ide orang lain.

examples.en: He's so stingy that he never pays for coffee.
examples.id: Dia pelit sekali sampai tidak pernah membayar kopi.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Budi cooks at home, compares prices and saved enough for a house deposit at 30. At his farewell party, his manager praises him.

question.prompt: 'Budi is very ___, and that's why he could buy a house so young.' Which word fits the manager's praise?
question.explanation: The manager is praising Budi, so he needs the positive word: **thrifty** (hemat). **stingy** and **mean** (pelit) describe the same habit as a fault.

steps.title: More words on the line
steps.text: Here are more pairs to know, each from positive to negative.
steps.body: Some depend on context. **cheap** is fine for prices (*cheap flights*), but about things it often means badly made (murahan). **childlike** is positive (innocent, full of wonder); **childish** is negative. **famous** is for things people admire; **notorious** for something bad. And **youthful** (awet muda) is positive, **young** neutral, **immature** (belum dewasa) negative. Also: **economical** = hemat (*ekonomis*), but **economic** = about the economy.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Bu Ani is telling the director about a new intern, and she's clearly impressed.

question.prompt: 'Our new intern is very ___: she asks smart questions about every project and has read all our old reports.' Which word fits?
question.explanation: Bu Ani is impressed, and the questions are about work: **curious** (ingin tahu) is the positive word. **nosy** (kepo) is negative: asking about things that aren't your business. **pushy** means forcing people, which doesn't fit asking questions.

steps.title: Say what's good about it
steps.text: Now the second skill: replacing vague words with precise ones.
steps.body:
Indonesian *bagus* and English **good** cover almost everything, so reports full of *good, bad, big, thing* sound vague. Ask **what exactly** is good: does it work (**effective**), work every time (**reliable**), help a lot (**valuable**), do someone good (**beneficial**)? `The new method is very good` → **The new method is highly effective.**

Also: **thing** → **issue** (a problem), **factor** (a reason), **aspect**, **item**. **get** → **obtain**, **receive**, **gain** (experience).

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina is writing her yearly supplier report: 'Our courier, Kilat Express, is very good: in two years, every parcel has arrived on time.'

question.prompt: Which word is the most precise replacement for 'good' in Rina's sentence?
question.explanation: Every parcel on time for two years = it works every time: **reliable** (andal). **beneficial** means good for someone's health or situation; **extensive** means covering a wide area, so it can't replace good here.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Sari's manager says 'a big impact' sounds vague in her report. Use the precise word instead.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Pelatihan itu berdampak signifikan pada penjualan.
question.solution: The training had a significant impact on sales.
question.explanation: **significant** (signifikan) is the precise word for an important change or effect, and **a significant impact on** is a natural partnership. 'big' only says size and sounds vague in a report.

steps.title: Match the tone
steps.text: Last skill: choosing words that fit what the text is for.
steps.body:
- **Reference letter**: praise: *reliable, determined, a quick learner*.
- **Complaint**: **firm but polite**: *I was disappointed that …, I would like a refund.* No insults, and not so soft that it sounds optional (*no worries if not!*).
- **News report**: **neutral**: *said, demonstrators, the government*.
- **Performance review**: **constructive**: *could check the figures more carefully*, not *lazy*.

**Euphemisms** are softer, polite words. They're kind, but they can also hide what really happened.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: The air conditioning in Pak Hasan's hotel room in Yogyakarta didn't work for two nights. He writes to the hotel manager.

question.prompt: Which sentence fits a firm but polite complaint?
options: I was disappointed that the air conditioning in my room did not work for two nights, and I would like a partial refund.
Your hotel is a disaster and your staff are useless. I want my money back now.
Sorry to bother you! The AC was a bit strange, but no worries if you can't do anything!
question.explanation: A good complaint says clearly what went wrong and what you want, politely: **I was disappointed that …, I would like …**. The second insults the staff; the third is so soft that the hotel can easily ignore it.

steps.title: Read more
steps.text: Two short articles about connotation, from VOA Learning English and the Cambridge Dictionary blog, if you'd like more examples.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini tentang memilih kata yang benar-benar tepat: kata yang artinya sama tapi rasanya berbeda, kata yang presisi sebagai ganti kata yang samar, dan kata yang cocok dengan nada sebuah teks. Kita mulai dari 'rasa' di balik sebuah kata.

steps.title: Arti sama, rasa berbeda
steps.text: Di B2 kamu memilih kata formal atau informal sesuai pembacanya. Sekarang kata-katanya sama formalnya, tapi rasanya berbeda.
steps.body:
**Konotasi** (connotation) = 'rasa' atau nilai yang dibawa sebuah kata di luar arti kamusnya: **positif**, **netral** atau **negatif**. Kamu sudah kenal dari bahasa Indonesia: *langsing*, *kurus* dan *kurus kering* bisa menggambarkan tubuh yang sama, tapi hanya *langsing* yang terdengar sebagai pujian. *Hemat* memuji; *pelit* mengkritik kebiasaan yang sama.

Jebakannya: kamus atau Google Translate memberi *kurus → thin, skinny, slim* tanpa rasanya. Salah pilih, kamu bisa menyinggung orang tanpa sadar.

steps.title: Memuji atau mengkritik?
steps.text: Ini kata-kata tadi dalam kalimat nyata. Perhatikan mana yang memuji dan mana yang mengkritik.
steps.body: `Our manager is stubborn, which really helps the team` mengirim dua pesan sekaligus: **stubborn** mengkritik, tapi sisa kalimatnya memuji. Pakai **firm**. Hati-hati: **mean** = pelit dalam bahasa Inggris British, tapi dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika biasanya berarti *tidak baik hati*.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Budi suka masak di rumah, membandingkan harga, dan sudah menabung cukup untuk uang muka rumah di usia 30. Di acara perpisahannya, manajernya memujinya.

question.prompt: 'Budi is very ___, and that's why he could buy a house so young.' Kata mana yang cocok untuk pujian manajernya?
question.explanation: Manajernya sedang memuji Budi, jadi butuh kata yang positif: **thrifty** (hemat). **stingy** dan **mean** (pelit) menggambarkan kebiasaan yang sama sebagai kekurangan.

steps.title: Lebih banyak kata di garis yang sama
steps.text: Ini pasangan lain yang perlu kamu tahu, masing-masing dari positif ke negatif.
steps.body: Sebagian tergantung konteks. **cheap** wajar untuk harga (*cheap flights*), tapi untuk barang sering berarti dibuat asal-asalan (murahan). **childlike** positif (polos, penuh rasa kagum); **childish** negatif. **famous** untuk hal yang dikagumi; **notorious** untuk hal yang buruk. Lalu **youthful** (awet muda) positif, **young** netral, **immature** (belum dewasa) negatif. Juga: **economical** = hemat (*ekonomis*), sedangkan **economic** = berkaitan dengan ekonomi.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bu Ani sedang bercerita kepada direktur tentang anak magang baru, dan dia jelas terkesan.

question.prompt: 'Our new intern is very ___: she asks smart questions about every project and has read all our old reports.' Kata mana yang cocok?
question.explanation: Bu Ani terkesan, dan pertanyaannya tentang pekerjaan: **curious** (ingin tahu) adalah kata yang positif. **nosy** (kepo) negatif: bertanya tentang hal yang bukan urusanmu. **pushy** berarti suka memaksa orang, tidak cocok untuk mengajukan pertanyaan.

steps.title: Sebutkan apa yang bagus
steps.text: Sekarang keterampilan kedua: mengganti kata yang samar dengan kata yang presisi.
steps.body:
*Bagus* dalam bahasa Indonesia dan **good** dalam bahasa Inggris dipakai untuk hampir semua hal, jadi laporan yang penuh *good, bad, big, thing* terdengar samar. Tanyakan **apa tepatnya** yang bagus: apakah berhasil (**effective**), selalu berfungsi (**reliable**), sangat berguna (**valuable**), bermanfaat bagi seseorang (**beneficial**)? `The new method is very good` → **The new method is highly effective.**

Juga: **thing** → **issue** (masalah), **factor** (alasan), **aspect**, **item**. **get** → **obtain**, **receive**, **gain** (pengalaman).

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina sedang menulis laporan tahunan tentang pemasok: 'Our courier, Kilat Express, is very good: in two years, every parcel has arrived on time.'

question.prompt: Kata mana yang paling presisi untuk mengganti 'good' di kalimat Rina?
question.explanation: Semua paket tepat waktu selama dua tahun = selalu berfungsi: **reliable** (andal). **beneficial** berarti baik untuk kesehatan atau keadaan seseorang; **extensive** berarti mencakup wilayah yang luas, jadi tidak bisa mengganti good di sini.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Manajer Sari bilang 'a big impact' terdengar samar di laporannya. Pakai kata yang lebih presisi.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Pelatihan itu berdampak signifikan pada penjualan.
question.solution: The training had a significant impact on sales.
question.explanation: **significant** (signifikan) adalah kata yang presisi untuk perubahan atau dampak yang penting, dan **a significant impact on** adalah pasangan kata yang alami. 'big' hanya menyebut ukuran dan terdengar samar di laporan.

steps.title: Sesuaikan nadanya
steps.text: Keterampilan terakhir: memilih kata yang cocok dengan tujuan teksnya.
steps.body:
- **Surat rekomendasi**: memuji: *reliable, determined, a quick learner*.
- **Keluhan**: **tegas tapi sopan**: *I was disappointed that …, I would like a refund.* Tanpa hinaan, dan jangan terlalu lunak sampai terdengar tidak wajib (*no worries if not!*).
- **Berita**: **netral**: *said, demonstrators, the government*.
- **Penilaian kinerja**: **membangun**: *could check the figures more carefully*, bukan *lazy*.

**Eufemisme** adalah kata yang lebih halus dan sopan. Kata-kata ini baik hati, tapi juga bisa menyembunyikan apa yang sebenarnya terjadi.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: AC di kamar hotel Pak Hasan di Yogyakarta tidak berfungsi selama dua malam. Dia menulis kepada manajer hotel.

question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang cocok untuk keluhan yang tegas tapi sopan?
options: I was disappointed that the air conditioning in my room did not work for two nights, and I would like a partial refund.
Your hotel is a disaster and your staff are useless. I want my money back now.
Sorry to bother you! The AC was a bit strange, but no worries if you can't do anything!
question.explanation: Keluhan yang baik menyebut dengan jelas apa yang salah dan apa yang kamu minta, dengan sopan: **I was disappointed that …, I would like …**. Kalimat kedua menghina stafnya; kalimat ketiga terlalu lunak sehingga hotel bisa dengan mudah mengabaikannya.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman: garis sinonim, kata yang presisi, dan alat untuk mengatur nada.
